messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: P0 fired — inference-prod: 5xx spike on model-serving cluster (alert: error-rate > 5% for 2m)

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1845 — assigned to alex (primary oncall) · paging alex now

alex: acked — I'm on it. grabbing logs and tailing the GPU nodes.

mira: on standby, will watch autoscaler and GPU utilization. can you paste the pod list?

alex: quick dump of failing pods: ```
kubectl get pods -n inference-prod | grep CrashLoop || true
inference-svc-5c7d8   1/1 Running   3 (3h ago)  23m
model-worker-7f9c2    0/1 CrashLoopBackOff  4 (5m ago)  6m
routing-proxy-2b1a4   1/1 Running   0 (20m ago)  24m
```

jordan: seeing similar in cloudwatch — sudden increase in 5xx for route /v1/generate, looks like a KV cache pressure leading to OOMs on worker pods.

kevin: any customer-impact yet? Support dashboard shows uptick in errors for customer "BrightByte" but they haven't filed a ticket.

alex: confirmed BRIGHTBYTE experiencing errors on their single-tenant Dedicated pool. I'm rolling traffic to fallback model for that tenant. doing a canary switch now.

oncall-bot: auto-grouping detected 18 alerts in 30s from same resource. Consolidating into alert group AG-9921 to avoid paging storm.

pagerduty-bot: alex acknowledged the incident at 1850004353. Escalation timer paused.

mira: looks like disk pressure on instance gpu-12, evicting cache entries. I'm increasing KV cache eviction aggressiveness (flip flag kv.cache.eviction=aggressive). patching now.

alex: command I ran to flip the flag on the deployment: ```
kubectl -n inference-prod set env deployment/model-worker KV_CACHE_EVICTION=aggressive
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-worker
```

jordan: after restart we see immediate drop in OOMs and 5xx back to baseline for most routes. still watching brightbyte traffic.

kevin: BrightByte confirms reduced errors on their side — they see requests succeed again. I'll ping customer and mark high-priority support message as resolved if they confirm in 10m.

alex: putting a temporary silence on noisy alerts for the grouped alert to stop duplicates. ```/pagerduty silence AG-9921 30m --reason "mitigation in progress; auto-dedupe on"```

oncall-bot: Applied suppression: AG-9921 silenced for 30m. Note: this will not suppress new unique alerts (different resource id).

pagerduty-bot: Silence created by alex (30m) — alerts deduplicated. Reminder: if incident continues past 25m, escalation will resume.

mira: also increased autoscaler headroom by +1 replica as a precaution. ```
kubectl -n inference-prod scale deployment/model-worker --replicas=6```
Scaling initiated.

jordan: adding note — we should tune the alert to consider cache-overtype conditions; current threshold triggers a paging storm for transient spikes. Propose: add 60s grace window and aggregate by resource group.

alex: agreed. I'll open a follow-up ticket for alert tuning and postmortem. For now, monitoring looks stable.

kevin: I'll keep BrightByte notified and file a customer-impact note on the ticket.

oncall-bot: housekeeping: grouped alerts older than 1h will be auto-archived; duplicate suppression window 5m. If you need permanent suppression, create an alert suppression rule in the console (ops -> alerts -> suppressions).

alex: incident acknowledged and mitigated — switching to maintenance mode. handoff to mira for longer-term checks. I'm logging the timeline in INC-2026-1845.

mira: taking over oncall for validation and post-incident actions. planning to: 1) keep silence for 30m, 2) collect kube-eviction logs, 3) run memory/kv profiling on model-worker, 4) propose alert tuning.

jordan: adding to postmortem checklist: exact trigger, whether eviction was cause or symptom, and a rollback plan for kv changes.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-1845 status: mitigated (acknowledged -> mitigated) by alex at 1850004690.

kevin: marking support case as monitoring — will escalate if BrightByte reports anything else.

alex: final note — the auto-grouping helped avoid a paging storm. we should consider lowering grouping sensitivity for customer-dedicated pools to avoid hiding single-tenant P0s. opened ticket TKT-9812.

mira: thanks everyone. will run follow-up during our 2pm reliability sync.

oncall-bot: This thread will be auto-closed after 24h of inactivity. If you add follow-up comments, the timestamps will update.
